heading: The most expensive loan you can take
The Minimum Amount Due trap
points: Pay only the minimum → no late fee, account stays regular
But interest keeps running on the full balance
No interest-free period on new purchases until fully paid
Interest is charged from the date of each transaction

heading: ₹1,00,000 unpaid for 12 months
note: Illustrative: 3.6% p.m. interest + ₹1,300 late fee each month + 18% GST. Actual rates vary by bank.

items.text: Paying one card's bill with another card
1–3% fee on every rotation (wallet / rent-pay / cash)
Debt only moves — it never shrinks
Loan apps to pay cards: higher interest + worse harassment

title: Due date missed — the 3-day window
items: RBI: no late fee if paid within 3 days of the due date
RBI: cannot be reported as 'past due' to CIBIL in these 3 days
Interest may still apply
Reminder SMS & e-mails begin

title: Late fee & interest kick in
items: Late fee ₹100 to ₹1,300+ (slab-based) + GST
Interest on the entire balance
Reminder calls and SMS from the bank
DPD (Days Past Due) reported — score starts falling

title: Second due date missed
items: In-house collection team calls several times a day
Card usually blocked for new spends
30+ DPD on credit report — score drops sharply
Another late fee, more interest

title: SMA-2 — one step before NPA
items: Account tagged SMA-2 (61–90 days overdue)
Case often handed to an external recovery agency
'Final reminder' letters and notices
WhatsApp messages; home visits may start

title: Account becomes NPA
items: NPA = Non-Performing Asset
Card permanently blocked / closed
Default can stay on credit report up to 7 years
Settlement offers start appearing

title: Write-off ≠ forgiveness
items: Bank may 'write off' in its books (accounting only)
The debt is NOT forgiven — recovery continues
Legal notice / Lok Adalat / arbitration notice possible
Deeper settlement discounts often possible

title: Court stage (possible, not certain)
items: Civil recovery suit can be filed
Limitation: 3 years — restarts on part-payment or written acknowledgement
NEVER ignore a court summons
No response → decision can be passed in your absence

can: Charge interest & late fees (as per terms)
Call & remind you (8 AM – 7 PM only)
Set-off dues from your account in the SAME bank
Go to court / arbitration / Lok Adalat
cannot: Seize property without a court order
Call before 8 AM or after 7 PM
Threaten, abuse or shame you publicly
Tell your relatives, friends or office about your debt
Charge over-limit fees without your consent

headline: Card default is a CIVIL matter
sub: Not a crime. No FIR, no arrest — just for not paying.

exceptions.text: A cheque you gave bounces (Sec 138, NI Act)
Bank-account auto-debit / NACH bounces (Sec 25, PSS Act)
Fraud from day one — fake documents / identity

items.text: Non-stop calls from many numbers
Calls to family, friends, office, references
Fake 'legal notice' PDFs on WhatsApp
"Police will come" · "Arrest warrant" · "FIR tomorrow"
Posing as advocate, police or court officer
Group visits to home / office to shame you

messages: ⚠️ FINAL WARNING: Legal action will be initiated against you within 24 HOURS.
Arrest warrant has been issued in your name. Pay TODAY to avoid police action.
Our field team will visit your HOME and OFFICE tomorrow.
Your photo will be shared with all your contacts.

pairs: Non-payment alone is civil. No arrest, no FIR.
Only a COURT issues warrants — after a proper summons, not WhatsApp.
Agents have zero such power. Only a court decree & process.
Only a court order can. Agents can't shame you to your employer.
Small payments close nothing. Pay only to the bank's official account, with a written plan.

heading: Recovery agent rules
source: RBI circular, 12 Aug 2022 · Outsourcing & Fair Practices directions
items: No calls before 8 AM or after 7 PM
No intimidation, abuse, threats or public humiliation
No intrusion into privacy of family, friends, referees
No anonymous / threatening calls or abusive social-media messages
No false or misleading statements
The BANK is responsible for its agents' conduct

heading: Credit card rules
source: RBI Master Direction — Credit & Debit Cards (Issuance and Conduct), 2022
items: No late fee or 'past due' reporting until 3 days after due date
No interest on unpaid fees & charges (no capitalisation)
No over-limit charges without your explicit consent
Minimum due must not make the debt keep growing
After settlement: bank must update CIBIL within 30 days

items.text: Screenshot every message — number, date, time
Log every call: date, time, number, name
Record calls where possible
Ask visitors for ID + bank authorisation letter
Talk to the bank only by e-mail

cards.line: Please send everything in writing to my registered e-mail. I will respond there.
Disclosing someone's loan to others is against RBI rules. This call is recorded. Don't call this number again.
Show your ID and the bank's authorisation letter. I'll deal with the bank in writing. Please leave now.

tip: Stay calm · Don't argue · Never get physical

heading: 7-step action plan
steps: Stop using the card — stop rotation
List every debt: balance, min. due, due date, rate
Protect essentials: rent, food, medicine, auto-debit EMIs
E-mail the bank early: EMI conversion / restructuring
Explain your hardship honestly — in writing
Plan a lump sum for settlement
Never take app loans to pay card dues

left.title: Before 90 days
items: EMI conversion / restructuring possible
Lower interest plans
Less damage to credit score

right.title: After NPA (90+ days)
items: Settlement: pay less than owed
'Settled' tag on CIBIL
New loans hard for years

heading: Settlement checklist
items: Negotiate on the principal — in writing, with the bank
Get the settlement letter on bank letterhead BEFORE paying
Letter must show amount, account no. & 'full and final settlement'
Pay ONLY to the bank's official account / link — never agent UPI or cash
Collect the No-Dues Certificate (NOC)
Check your CIBIL report after 30–45 days

heading: 'Settled' is not 'Closed'
items: 'Settled' = you paid less than owed → lenders see it as negative
Later, pay the waived amount → status can become 'Closed'
Rebuild: on-time payments, low usage, time

items.text: Never ignore court / Lok Adalat notices — attend or reply via advocate
Never share OTP, card details or Aadhaar with callers
Beware 'settlement companies' taking big upfront fees
Never sign blank or unread papers
Salary in the same bank as card dues? Understand set-off risk
Default is civil — not a crime. But don't ignore it.
Talk to the bank before 90 days
Everything in writing
Harassment? RBI rules are on your side
Settle only with a letter first
